title: obsidian-tc HTTP transport lacks Origin/DNS-rebinding protection, enabling drive-by vault access on loopback
description:
Impact
The Streamable HTTP transport was constructed without enableDnsRebindingProtection/allowedHosts/allowedOrigins and performed no Origin-header validation. With the documented auth.mode: "none" loopback default, a drive-by web page could POST http://127.0.0.1/mcp and receive caller http-local with scopes ["*"] — full vault read/write — via DNS rebinding / a forged Origin.

Patches
Fixed in 1.3.1. Upgrade to >= 1.3.1. The transport now enables DNS-rebinding protection and allowed hosts/origins and returns HTTP 403 on an invalid Origin (per MCP 2025-11-25).

Workarounds
Do not expose the HTTP transport with auth.mode: "none"; require JWT auth, or bind to a non-loopback interface behind a proxy that validates Origin.

recommended_sla_action: URGENT PATCH — Critical severity, deploy fix within 72 hours

title: obsidian-tc tokens can access arbitrary configured vaults
description:
Impact
Tool dispatch did not check the caller-supplied input.vault against the caller's bound vault (ctx.vaultId); the folder ACL was a single global instance and the JWT carried no vault claim. As a result, any valid token could read, write, or delete any configured vault by passing input.vault, defeating multi-tenant isolation across ~90 tool sites. (resources/read was the only surface that already guarded this.)

Patches
Fixed in 1.3.1 (the fix was developed on the v1.3.0 tag, which never published to npm; 1.3.1 is the first published release with the fix). Upgrade to >= 1.3.1.

Workarounds
Run a single vault per server process, or isolate each tenant on a separate process/credential.

Fix
A central input.vault === ctx.vaultId guard was added in dispatch before the scope check.

title: undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via unhandled error on excessive content-encodings
description:
Impact

undici's fetch() crashes the Node.js process when a malicious server returns a response with more than five content codings and closes the connection before sending the body. undici rejects such responses (a content-encoding limit), but it created the internal response stream before that check and returned without attaching an error listener or aborting the request. The early close then surfaces a content-length mismatch on that orphaned internal stream, which Node.js treats as an unhandled error and terminates the process. A remote, unauthenticated server can trigger this with a single response, even when the application correctly catches the fetch() rejection. undici 6.x, 7.x, and 8.x are affected.

Patches

Upgrade to 6.29.1, 7.30.1, or 8.12.2. undici now validates the content-encoding chain before creating the internal body stream and aborts the response when the limit is exceeded, so no error can surface on an orphaned stream.

Workarounds

None.

recommended_sla_action: SCHEDULED PATCH — Apply in next maintenance window

title: Pillow: MSP RLE decoder expands a tiny file into unbounded memory
description:

title: undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via unbounded memory in the EventSource parser
description:
Impact

undici's EventSource client can be driven to exhaust process memory by a malicious or compromised Server-Sent Events peer. By sending millions of tiny completed data: fields with no blank event separator, or a single unfinished line split across many chunks, the parser retains a growing amount of per-field and per-chunk state. The byte-based maxEventSize and maxResponseSize limits do not bound that retained state, and maxResponseSize is enforced on the compressed body before decompression, so a small compressed response can expand into enough retained memory to terminate the process. The application only needs to maintain an EventSource connection to an untrusted peer, which controls only the response. Availability is the only impact.

Upgrade to 6.29.1, 7.30.1, or 8.12.2, which bound the retained EventSource parser state (the number of data fields and buffered chunks, the unfinished-line length, and per-field byte totals) independently of the byte limits.

title: undici vulnerable to Subresource Integrity bypass via non-lowercase algorithm tokens
description:
Impact

undici's fetch() verifies Subresource Integrity (SRI) metadata by looking up the algorithm token in a lowercase-only set, but the SRI specification defines a valid token by its ASCII-lowercase form. A correct but non-lowercase token such as SHA256-... or Sha256-... is therefore treated as unknown and skipped. title: Pillow: Quadratic GIF comment concatenation allows DoS in Image.open()
description:

Location: src/PIL/GifImagePlugin.py:266  in GifImageFile._seek()

============================================================================

Opening a crafted GIF file with Image.open() takes time that grows with the square of the file's size, so anyone who can submit an image to a service that uses Pillow can keep one worker busy at full processor load for a long time with a small file. title: Pillow tiled-TIFF decoder reads past tile buffer in copy4 (Unpack.c:1290)
description:
Summary

Pillow's libImaging _decodeTile decoder, used to decode tiled TIFF images, allocates a per-tile buffer using realloc(state->buffer, TIFFTileSize(tiff)). After each TIFFReadTile it then iterates tile_y from 0 up to current_tile_length and calls the configured row unpacker (here copy4) with the source pointer state->buffer + tile_y * row_byte_size. When libtiff returns a tile_bytes_size smaller than the worst-case row_byte_size * tile_length, the inner stride-and-copy loop walks past the realloc'd region and copy4 performs a 1024-byte memcpy that reads up to (tile_length-1) * row_byte_size + row_byte_size bytes from a buffer sized only to tile_bytes_size. The supplied PoC TIFF triggers a 1024-byte over-read exactly 0 bytes past a 196608-byte allocation. An attacker who can convince a Pillow-using application to decode a crafted TIFF can trigger a process crash (DoS) and may cause adjacent heap memory to be copied into the decoded pixel buffer.

title: markdown-it: Quadratic-time denial of service in inline HTML parsing with html enabled
description:
Summary

With html: true, markdown-it takes quadratic time to parse repeated unterminated HTML constructs inside a paragraph. This affects HTML comments (<!--), processing instructions (<?), declarations (<!A), and CDATA sections (<![CDATA[).

An attacker-controlled input of a few hundred kilobytes can block the Node.js event loop for seconds or tens of seconds. The default configuration has HTML disabled, but the commonmark preset enables it.

The issue was reported against the published markdown-it@15.0.2 package on Node.js 20 and reproduced on the current source with Node.js 24.16.0.

Details

src/rules_inline/text.ts treats < as a terminator, causing the inline parser to attempt the HTML rule at successive HTML construct openers.

With HTML enabled, src/rules_inline/html_inline.ts applies an anchored regular expression to the remaining input:

const match = state.src.slice(pos).match(HTML_TAG_RE)

title: ApostropheCMS: Unauthenticated resource exhaustion via pre-auth aposBigUpload processing in @apostrophecms/import-export
description:
Summary

A potential unauthenticated denial-of-service vulnerability exists in the chunked import upload path used by @apostrophecms/import-export.

The affected import API routes invoke:

self.apos.http.bigUploadMiddleware()

before the actual import handler performs its authentication check.

Because no authorize callback is supplied to bigUploadMiddleware(), unauthenticated requests can reach the aposBigUpload start, chunk, and end operations before the later req.user check rejects the import.

As a result, an unauthenticated remote attacker can create server-side upload state, write chunk data to upload storage, trigger temporary-file processing, and cause attacker-controlled cleanup operations before authentication is enforced.

Package:

@apostrophecms/import-export

Confirmed affected version:

3.6.2

title: MCP TypeScript SDK: One HTTP request within the default size limit could exhaust server memory during validation
description:
Summary
In affected versions, servers put no limit on how many array elements and object keys they validated in one request. One HTTP request within the default 4 MiB size limit could exhaust the server's memory, and the process aborted with JavaScript heap out of memory.

No credentials are needed, unless you authenticate requests before they reach the SDK.

Am I affected?
Yes, if clients you do not fully trust can reach your server over HTTP. The risk is highest for McpServer tools whose input contains an array or a record. stdio-only servers are not affected.

- @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.3.0 through 1.31.0
- @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.0.0 through 2.2.0

Upgrade to:

- 2.x: @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.3.0 or later

title: launch-editor: fs.existsSync() existence check can be bypassed on Windows
description:
Summary

launch-editor checked fs.existsSync(fileName) before passing a supplied path to an editor command. On Windows, an attacker can bypass this check with a crafted path ending in \\..:line:column. This removes the requirement that the attacker be able to place a file with a malicious filename.

Combined with the % escaping issue described in GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv (https://github.com/vitejs/launch-editor/security/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv), this bypass can lead to OS command injection when an attacker controls the file argument.

Impact

Only apps that runs on Windows is affected.

Details

title: filelock: ReadWriteLock on Windows acts on SQLite side files another local user places beside its database
description:
On Windows, ReadWriteLock and AsyncReadWriteLock (the SQLite-backed reader/writer lock) connect SQLite to the lock database by its path, in every directory. title: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow in ImagingJpegDecode

JpegImageFile.draft() — which Image.thumbnail() calls automatically — requests 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 scaled JPEG output and shrinks self._size and the tile extents to match, so _setimage() allocates a single-row decode buffer of ceil(W/s) samples. Each jpeg_read_scanlines() call writes (W - ceil(W/s)) x components bytes past the end of the heap allocation, and the overflowing bytes are the decoded pixel values, which are byte-exact for an 8-bit grayscale lossless image.

description:

title: ApostropheCMS: The general public can access @apostrophecms/user objects via a relationship (viewRole is not applied to the general public)
description:
Impact
Even though it is correctly applied to guests, contributors, etc., viewRole is not applied to the general public. This means that a secured content type like @apostrophecms/user can in theory be accessed.

This is greatly mitigated by the fact that there is no automatic public REST API for any content type. One has to expressly allow it. However, it does mean that developers can make the mistake of setting up a relationship between a content type like a blog post, and @apostrophecms/user. This could potentially expose some sensitive information if templates were written poorly, e.g. if they JSON-serialized the entire object. Note that password hashes are NOT affected because they reside in a separate collection.

The public demo project and its various flavors must be updated first because it inadvertently relies on the bug.
